pinned_source.title: Universal Sequencing on an Unreliable Machine
pinned_source.summarized_original_work: Epstein, Levin, Marchetti-Spaccamela, Megow, Mestre, Skutella, and Stougie (2012), Universal sequencing on a single unreliable machine, SIAM Journal on Computing 41(3), 565–586, DOI 10.1137/110844210.
pinned_source.license: No source-code license asserted; clean-room implementation of the chapter's mathematical algorithm

input.total_weight_rule: The sum of all weights must be a power of two in 1..32, matching the chapter's displayed level range and making its top capacity include every job.

contract.algorithm: For each i=0..log2(total_weight), choose a maximum-total-processing subset under weight capacity 2^i; append each job at its lowest selected level, with levels descending.
contract.knapsack_tie_breaking: For equal processing totals choose the numerically smallest membership mask, where job 0 is the least significant bit.
contract.within_level_order: Append job IDs in ascending order.
contract.profile_scope: Sequence construction only; no unreliable-machine simulation or schedule-cost calculation. Exact integer 0/1 dynamic programming is used for each level.

workspace.meaning: Fixed arrays for twelve jobs, six knapsack levels, exact-weight DP through capacity 32, and a staged 104-byte output.
